clue.text: It could fall on the south this instant

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for south
this instant means right now, at present

explanation.surface: A forecaster warns that something could come down over southern parts at any moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Winter precipitation is something that falls from the sky, so the vague 'it could fall' covers it.

clue.text: Go for an injection

explanation.surface: Someone at the clinic is told to go ahead and have a jab.
explanation.definitionFit: A go is an attempt or try, as in 'have a go'; a jab from a needle is a medical dose given by syringe.

clue.text: Goes topless in such vessels

indicators.note: topless says the word loses its top, which in a down entry is its first letter

parts.note: goes, as in taking goes in a game, are turns

explanation.surface: Someone strips off their top half in some sort of boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the first letter T from TURNS. 'Goes' is a plural noun here (a go is a turn), not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are vases or containers, a kind of vessel for holding liquid or ashes.

clue.text: Cora due to be relocated in the country

indicators.note: relocated means moved to a new place, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman called Cora is about to move abroad to a new land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be relocated' rearranges the letters of CORA and DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecuador is a South American nation, an example of a country.

clue.text: Retailer with stocks of tea

parts.note: cha is a colloquial word for tea
having stocks of something means having it in store, kept in reserve

explanation.surface: A shop is described by its well-stocked tea supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'with stocks of tea' as tea in store: CHA plus IN STORE, the order the phrase would take in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A multiple shop with many branches selling goods is a kind of retail business.

clue.text: Not the way to serve whisky when destitute

definitions.text: Not the way to serve whisky

explanation.surface: A purist complains about ice in drinks while someone else has fallen on hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: Whisky purists insist that ice spoils a good malt, so the clue calls serving it over ice the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Over ice cubes is how some drinkers take spirits; a person or business in ruin is said to be in that state too.

clue.text: Points to case initially stacked with drugs

parts.note: points of the compass: S and E, south and east
the dative is a grammatical case, used for indirect objects

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the following word, stacked

explanation.surface: Someone points to a briefcase packed with pharmaceuticals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' are compass points (south, east); 'case' is grammar, not luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedatives are calming medicines, one kind of drug.

clue.text: Pale and a little self-effacing

parts.note: slightly self-effacing describes a bashful, timid person

explanation.surface: Someone is described as wan and somewhat retiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash-coloured means greyish and wan, so a pallid face can be described this way.

clue.text: Arranging sale again proves no pain

indicators.note: arranging means putting in a new order, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: Organising a second sale turns out to be painless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranging' rearranges the letters of SALE and AGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is medical relief from pain, an absence of feeling it.

clue.text: Bear displayed on a pedestal?

explanation.surface: A bear is put on show standing on a plinth.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: something set on a pedestal comes with a stand, read as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear is to endure or resist; an exhibit set on a plinth comes 'with stand' in the split reading.

clue.text: In Lesotho temperatures are scorching

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words Lesotho temperatures

explanation.surface: A weather report from southern Africa says it is baking.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorching weather is extremely warm, a synonym.

clue.text: Keen for sextet to appear in billing

indicators.note: to appear in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: billing as in publicity: an ad advertises
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An eager group of six musicians want top billing on the poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and eager are synonyms, describing enthusiasm.

clue.text: A large lake, and nothing more

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A big lake, and that is the whole of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'that's it' means nothing more follows: the whole lot, the entirety.

clue.text: Murderer had a close shave thereby

explanation.surface: A killer narrowly escaped capture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had a close shave' looks like a near miss, but means literally shaved with an open razor.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-throat is a violent killer; it is also a straight razor giving a very close shave.

clue.text: Airman and crew involved in major conflict

indicators.note: involved means tangled or mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Aircrew get caught up in a large-scale war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges the letters of AIRMAN and CREW.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean War of 1853-56 was a major conflict between Russia and an alliance including Britain and France.

clue.text: The old lady wants divine inspiration?

parts.note: Sophy is a woman's name, a form of Sophie

explanation.surface: An elderly woman seeks guidance from heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: theosophy claims knowledge of God through mystical insight.
explanation.definitionFit: Theosophy is a religious philosophy based on mystical insight into the divine.

clue.text: Pillows for bosses about to sleep

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: heads are bosses, those in charge
to rest is to sleep

explanation.surface: Managers about to nod off need cushions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to sleep' reads as 'on the point of dozing off', but 'about' is the container signal and 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Cushions supporting the head on a seat are like pillows.

clue.text: Struggle to breathe, so talk quietly

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly
P stands for piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone out of breath can only speak softly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp intake of breath when winded is a synonym for struggling for air.

clue.text: Sack fellow who fights arsonists

parts.note: to sack someone is to dismiss or fire them
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: An employer dismisses a man for battling fire-raisers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the job: he fights the blazes that fire-raisers start.
explanation.definitionFit: A firefighter tackles the blazes that arsonists set, so loosely battles their work.

clue.text: Pussy-footing is sadly so naïve

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Treading carefully around an issue is said to be regrettably innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges the letters of SO NAIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pussy-footing means avoiding commitment, a form of dodging or sidestepping.

clue.text: Village back in America needs capital

parts.note: VIL is an abbreviation for village

indicators.note: back means the little word in is turned round

parts.note: taken as written
US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: A village in the United States needs money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses IN to NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Vilnius is the capital city of Lithuania.

clue.text: Draws attention to man writing

parts.note: he is a man
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A man's writing gets noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear one's throat with a little cough, 'ahem', is a way of drawing attention.

clue.text: Bring back checks on art gallery

parts.note: reins check or restrain a horse
Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone returns to supervise an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: TATE is the name of the main national art galleries in Britain, such as Tate Modern.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone to a post is to bring them back.

clue.text: The head ducks as well

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word The

parts.note: a duck is a score of zero in cricket, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: The leader dodges as well.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricket score of nothing, so ducks are two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and in addition are synonyms of this short word.

clue.text: Unit gained first prize, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for gained first prize is said aloud

parts.note: to come first is to have won

explanation.surface: A unit won the top award, word has it.
explanation.definitionFit: A single unit is one, the number.

clue.text: Break for a biscuit

explanation.surface: A tea break comes with a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: To break is to crack; a ginger biscuit is a crisp brittle cookie named for the noise.

clue.text: A guy's gone wild in place of worship

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man has run off into a house of prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges the letters of A GUYS GONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synagogue is a Jewish house of worship.

clue.text: Aim to travel with a leading lawyer

parts.note: to go is to travel

indicators.note: leading means the first letter of the word lawyer

explanation.surface: Someone intends to travel with a top barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or objective is a target.

clue.text: Lady Jane is elderly

explanation.surface: Lady Jane is getting on.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Jane Grey was the 'nine days' queen' of England in 1553.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Jane Grey was briefly queen of England; grey hair is a sign of old age.

clue.text: No longer working as an officer in the tower

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
on means working, switched on

explanation.surface: An official who used to work at a fortress has retired.
explanation.walkthrough: An exon is one of four officers of the Yeomen of the Guard, the royal bodyguard associated with the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: An exon is a junior officer in the Yeomen of the Guard, the royal bodyguard.

clue.text: Cagney lost points for being secretive

indicators.note: lost means the letters are taken out of the actor's name

parts.note: N and E are compass points, north and east

explanation.surface: James Cagney lost points for keeping secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes NE (two compass points) from CAGNEY. James Cagney was a Hollywood actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Cagey means guarded and unwilling to reveal much, close-mouthed.

clue.text: Hot roll for man's best friend?

explanation.surface: A hot roll is offered to a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: A hot dog is a sausage in a roll; the question mark flags that the dog is a dachshund.
explanation.definitionFit: A sausage dog is a dachshund, a long breed; read literally it describes a hot dog in a bun.
